description: Given an integer array nums where exactly two elements appear once and all other elements appear twice, find the two elements that appear only once. Return them in any order. You must use O(1) extra space.
intuition: XOR is the hero here - it cancels out pairs, leaving only the two unique numbers XORed together. The trick is finding a bit where they differ, then using that bit to split all numbers into two groups, each containing exactly one unique number.
approach: XOR all numbers to get xor of the two unique numbers. Find any set bit in this XOR (a differing bit). Partition all numbers by this bit and XOR each group separately to isolate the two unique numbers.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: nums = [1,2,1,3,2,5]
Step 1: XOR all → 1^2^1^3^2^5 = 3^5 = 6 (binary 110)
Step 2: differingBit = 6 & (-6) = 6 & ...11111010 = 2 (binary 010)
Step 3: group by bit 1:
  bit set (2):   2,3,2 → xor = 3  (uniqueA=3)
  bit clear (0): 1,1,5 → xor = 5  (uniqueB=5)
Result: [3, 5]
explanation:
1. XOR all numbers; duplicates cancel out, leaving xor of the two unique numbers.
2. Find the lowest set bit using xor_all & (-xor_all). This bit differs between the two unique numbers.
3. Partition all numbers into two groups based on whether that bit is set.
4. XOR within each group: duplicates cancel, leaving one unique number per group.
hints: XOR of all elements gives you xor of the two unique numbers.
The two unique numbers differ in at least one bit. Use that bit to split numbers into two groups.
Each group contains exactly one unique number, which you can isolate with XOR.
